Fix double-width characters disappearing when wrapping
summary: The function now processes the input string from left to right, starts a new line whenever adding a character would exceed the supplied width, and returns the resulting lines in the same order as they appear in the text; previously it processed the string in reverse order, began counting from a position offset, and returned the lines in reverse order. As a result, for any given input the output list is the original left‑to‑right split instead of the reversed split, and empty lines occur only when a character itself exceeds the width rather than being shifted by the position argument.

summary: Style.update_link now builds _link_id by concatenating the next value from a global counter (starting at a random 24‑bit seed) with the hash of the meta attribute, instead of concatenating a random integer in the range 0‑999999 with that hash. Consequently, for the same inputs the _link_id field changes from a pseudo‑random six‑digit number to a monotonically increasing integer (e.g., from 403958 to 14167048 when meta is None, and from 403958 to 14167048 when meta is present), while the link and meta values remain unchanged.

fix(next_version): reset prerelease when token changes (#339)
summary: When next_version is called with part="prerelease" and a prerelease_token that differs from the current prerelease’s first identifier (e.g., switching from “beta” to “rc”), the method now returns a version whose prerelease is set to <prerelease_token>.1 and whose build is cleared, instead of incrementing the numeric suffix of the existing prerelease while preserving its identifier. This change occurs only when the version has a non‑None prerelease and the supplied prerelease_token does not match the existing prerelease token.

title: Fix string_to_int radix when alphabet_index is provided
summary: When an alphabet_index is supplied, string_to_int now computes the radix as len(alphabet_index) instead of len(alphabet), so the base used for conversion changes whenever the two lengths differ. Consequently, inputs such as "010" with alphabet ['0','1','2'] and index {'0':0,'1':1} yield 2 instead of 3, and "20" with alphabet ['0','1'] and index {'0':0,'1':1,'2':2} yield 6 instead of 4.

rs = RetryCallState(retry_object=Retrying(wait=0), fn=lambda: None, args=(), kwargs={}); Retrying(wait=0)._run_wait(rs); rs.upcoming_sleep

summary: The function now unconditionally calls self.wait(retry_state) and assigns the result to retry_state.upcoming_sleep. Previously, when self.wait was falsy (e.g., None, False, 0, or an empty list), the function skipped the call and set upcoming_sleep to 0.0. After the change, those same inputs cause a TypeError because the non‑callable value is invoked as a function, while callable wait objects continue to behave as before.

summary: When maxsplit==0 the function used to always yield the entire iterable as one group, so an empty input produced a single empty group ([[]]); now it yields a group only if the iterable is non‑empty, so empty inputs produce no output at all ([]). Revert "Fix humanize reporting 'a month' for 16-day differences"
Fix humanize reporting 'a month' for 16-day differences
summary: The change prevents rounding up to a month when the elapsed time is more than two weeks but less than a full month and no calendar month has fully passed; instead, it returns a weeks‑based description. Consequently, Arrow(2020,1,1).humanize(Arrow(2020,1,20)) now yields '2 weeks ago' rather than 'a month ago'.
